YOUR TASK: find the copying heads of a language model.

THE MODEL: its weights are those of a real trained language model. Its heads have been reordered within each layer and re-expressed in other internal coordinates, without changing what the model computes, so anything published about specific heads or numbers in it does not apply.

THE QUESTION: take 50 random tokens followed by the same 50 tokens again. For a head, at each position t in the second copy except the last, take its attention weight from position t to position t-50+1, which is the token just after the earlier copy of the current token. Its score is the average of that weight over those positions and over many random sequences. Name the 5 heads, out of all 144, that you judge to have the highest scores.

HOW YOU ARE SCORED: the number of heads you name that are among the 5 heads with the truly highest scores, measured by running the model. It is never run for you.

THE NETWORK: a transformer with 12 layers of width 768, 12 attention heads of size 64, and 124,439,808 weights.

Tensors (rows x columns):
  E: 50257 x 768 (one row per token, used for both input and output)
  P: 1024 x 768 (one row per position)
  F.scale, F.shift: 768
  and for each layer i from 0 to 11:
  Li.norm1.scale, Li.norm1.shift: 768
  Li.qkv.W: 768 x 2304, Li.qkv.b: 2304
  Li.out.W: 768 x 768, Li.out.b: 768
  Li.norm2.scale, Li.norm2.shift: 768
  Li.up.W: 768 x 3072, Li.up.b: 3072
  Li.down.W: 3072 x 768, Li.down.b: 768

The computation, for input tokens t_0 ... t_(n-1), with no start token added:
  x_j = E[t_j] + P[j]
  For each layer i in order:
    y_j = LN(x_j; Li.norm1)
    a_j = y_j @ Li.qkv.W + Li.qkv.b. Split a_j into q_j (entries 0-767), k_j (768-1535), v_j (1536-2303).
    For each head h from 0 to 11, take entries 64h to 64h+63 of q, k and v, and compute
      w_ji = softmax over i <= j of (q_j . k_i) / 8, then o_j = sum over i <= j of w_ji v_i
    c_j = the 12 heads' o_j joined in order (768 entries)
    x_j = x_j + c_j @ Li.out.W + Li.out.b
    z_j = LN(x_j; Li.norm2)
    x_j = x_j + gelu(z_j @ Li.up.W + Li.up.b) @ Li.down.W + Li.down.b
  x_j = LN(x_j; F)
  logits_j = x_j @ transpose(E), the scores for the token after position j.
LN(u; n) = (u - mean(u)) / sqrt(var(u) + 0.00001) * n.scale + n.shift, element by element, with the mean and population variance taken over the 768 entries of u.
gelu here is the standard smooth approximation of u * Phi(u), which differs from it by at most 0.0005.
The model's top token is the one with the largest logit; a tie goes to the lowest token ID.


WHAT YOU CAN USE: the weights of the 12 blocks, as 32-bit floats: for each layer i, Li.norm1.scale, Li.norm1.shift, Li.qkv.W, Li.qkv.b, Li.out.W, Li.out.b, Li.norm2.scale, Li.norm2.shift, Li.up.W, Li.up.b, Li.down.W and Li.down.b. The tables E and P and the final F.scale and F.shift are NOT available.

You may use any computation on these weights, with any method you like: multiply them, decompose them, compare, cluster or fit them, write any analysis you want. Two things are NOT allowed:
1. A forward pass: do not run the network or any of its layers (normalization, attention with its softmax, the MLP with its gelu) on any input, whether real, random or constructed, in code, in your head or on paper. Treating the weight matrices as linear-algebra objects (products, eigenvalues, singular vectors, applying one weight matrix to directions taken from other weights) is fine; simulating what the network does to an input is not.
2. Search: do not look anything up (there is no internet access in any case).

HOW YOU COMPUTE: you read the weights by running Python code. To run code, end your reply with a code block whose opening line is three backticks followed by the word python. We run it and reply with its printed output. Available: numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, PyTorch (CPU), pandas, sympy, networkx. Before your code runs, numpy is imported as np and W is a dict of the weight arrays by name: W['L5.qkv.W'] is 768 x 2304, W['L5.up.W'] is 768 x 3072, and so on, and they apply as in the computation above. There is nothing else to read (no other files, no network). Each run is a fresh process (nothing is kept between runs), may take up to 600 seconds, and its output is cut at 20,000 characters. You may run code up to 20 times. Each turn is a fresh call that replays your earlier replies and outputs, and your private reasoning is not kept, so write down in your reply whatever you want to remember.

HOW TO ANSWER: when you are done, end your reply with a code block whose opening line is three backticks followed by the word answer, with one head per line as layer.head, counting from 0, for example:

```answer
3.7
```
Name 5 heads. Your first reply with an answer block ends the task.


YOUR REPLY IN TURN 1:
I’ll first measure direct copying tendencies and alignment between each head’s query–key matrix and earlier heads’ value–output matrices. These products are invariant to changes of coordinates inside a head.

```python
import numpy as np
import torch
from threadpoolctl import threadpool_limits
threadpool_limits(8)
torch.set_num_threads(8)

d, r = 768, 64
heads = []
for l in range(12):
    scale = torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(W[f'L{l}.norm1.scale'])).float()
    qkv = torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(W[f'L{l}.qkv.W'])).float()
    out = torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(W[f'L{l}.out.W'])).float()
    # Linear factors only: centering and learned scale, without evaluating LN.
    effective = scale[:, None] * qkv
    effective = effective - effective.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
    for h in range(12):
        Q = effective[:, h*r:(h+1)*r].contiguous()
        K = effective[:, d+h*r:d+(h+1)*r].contiguous()
        V = effective[:, 2*d+h*r:2*d+(h+1)*r].contiguous()
        O = out[h*r:(h+1)*r, :].contiguous()
        GQ, GK, GV, GO = Q.T@Q, K.T@K, V.T@V, O@O.T
        na = torch.sqrt((GQ*GK).sum().clamp_min(1e-20)).item()
        nb = torch.sqrt((GV*GO).sum().clamp_min(1e-20)).item()
        heads.append(dict(l=l,h=h,Q=Q,K=K,V=V,O=O,GQ=GQ,GV=GV,
                          na=na,nb=nb,
                          qk=(Q*K).sum().item()/na,
                          ov=(V*O.T).sum().item()/nb))

pairs = []
for t, H in enumerate(heads):
    n = H['l']*12
    if not n:
        continue
    prior = heads[:n]
    VT = torch.cat([p['V'].T for p in prior],dim=0)
    OO = torch.cat([p['O'] for p in prior],dim=0)
    U = (VT@H['Q']).reshape(n,r,r)
    T = (OO@H['K']).reshape(n,r,r)
    GV = torch.stack([p['GV'] for p in prior])
    gram = T.transpose(1,2) @ (GV@T)
    pn = torch.sqrt((gram*H['GQ'][None,:,:]).sum((1,2)).clamp_min(1e-20))
    tr = (U*T).sum((1,2))
    match = tr/pn
    align = tr/(H['na']*torch.tensor([p['nb'] for p in prior]))
    for s in range(n):
        pairs.append((t,s,float(match[s]),float(align[s]),float(tr[s]),float(pn[s])))

def name(i):
    return f"{heads[i]['l']}.{heads[i]['h']}"
print("Head metrics: QK=trace(QK)/Frobenius; OV=trace(VO)/Frobenius.")
print("match=trace(QK @ VO_prior.T)/Frobenius(product); align=cosine(QK,VO_prior).")
print("head       QK       OV    best_match source   align")
for t,H in enumerate(heads):
    pp = [p for p in pairs if p[0]==t]
    if pp:
        p=max(pp,key=lambda x:x[2])
        print(f"{name(t):>5} {H['qk']:8.3f} {H['ov']:8.3f} {p[2]:11.3f} {name(p[1]):>6} {p[3]:7.4f}")
    else:
        print(f"{name(t):>5} {H['qk']:8.3f} {H['ov']:8.3f}")
print("\nTOP 45 CIRCUITS BY MATCH")
for t,s,m,a,tr,pn in sorted(pairs,key=lambda x:x[2],reverse=True)[:45]:
    print(f"{name(s):>5} -> {name(t):>5} match={m:7.3f} align={a:7.4f} targetOV={heads[t]['ov']:7.3f}")
print("\nTOP 25 CIRCUITS BY ALIGNMENT")
for t,s,m,a,tr,pn in sorted(pairs,key=lambda x:x[3],reverse=True)[:25]:
    print(f"{name(s):>5} -> {name(t):>5} match={m:7.3f} align={a:7.4f} targetOV={heads[t]['ov']:7.3f}")
```
